official_facts.ttl_measured_from: request start; refreshed on every hit
official_facts.input_tokens_meaning: tokens after the last breakpoint (uncached tail)

invalidation.tools: any tool definition change invalidates tools+system+messages
invalidation.messages: message change invalidates messages from the changed block on
invalidation.model: no cross-model reuse; a model change is a full miss

model_resolution: longest matching prefix of the request `model` string against the keys of `models` (so dated ids such as claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 resolve); no match → verdict UNDETERMINED with code MODEL_UNKNOWN, never CONFORMANT

token_estimator.rule: ceil(chars/4) where chars = len(json.dumps(tools, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False)) + sum(len(block.text)) over the text blocks of L1..L3
token_estimator.purpose: offline lower-bound estimate used by the linter; it tends to UNDER-count JSON-heavy tool schemas, so a prefix that passes the estimate is above the model minimum with margin
token_estimator.runtime_rule: a runtime that can call the count_tokens endpoint MUST use it; the estimate is for offline lint only

L0.name: tools
L0.stability: global (identical for every session of an agent version)
L0.content: the full deterministic tool registry: real definitions and deferred stubs (name + one-line description + minimal schema) for tools loaded on demand via a tool-search tool
L0.order_rule: the registry order is fixed by the agent build (declared order or lexicographic by name); the same set in a different order is a different prefix
forbidden: cache_control on any tool (the L1 breakpoint covers tools)
removing or adding a tool mid-session (use deferred stubs)
L0.breakpoint: none — covered by the L1 breakpoint

L1.name: static_system
L1.api_field: system[partition 1] — blocks up to and including the first block carrying cache_control
L1.stability: global (identical for every session of an agent version)
L1.content: the agent's static instructions: role, way of working, output format, tool-use policy

breakpoint.ttl_by_cadence: 5m when the agent's loop cadence is under 5 minutes and sessions are short (profile decides)

L2.name: project_knowledge
L2.api_field: system[partition 2] — blocks after L1 up to and including the second block carrying cache_control
L2.stability: per project version (changes only when the knowledge pack is re-released; the release is pinned by a content digest, never by a timestamp)
L2.content: CLAUDE.md router / mandates / skills INDEX (names + one-line descriptions), knowledge pack pinned by content digest
forbidden: full skill bodies loaded on demand (those go to L4)

breakpoint.ttl_by_cadence: 5m under the same condition as L1; never lower than L3

L3.name: session_metadata
L3.api_field: either system[partition 3] (placement `system-tail`) or the leading text block(s) of messages[0] (role user) up to and including the first block carrying cache_control (placement `messages-head`)
L3.stability: per session (constant from the first request of a session to the last)
L3.content: a small key: value record (or JSON object) with ONLY the keys in grammar.allowed_keys

grammar.form: JSON object, or one `key: value` pair per non-empty line
grammar.uuid_rule: a UUID is permitted only as the value of an allowed key (a Muneral work item id is a UUID); any other UUID in L3 is DYN_UUID

L4.name: messages
L4.api_field: messages (after the L3 block(s) when placement is messages-head)
L4.stability: append-only within a session: request n's messages are a prefix of request n+1's messages (equality allowed for a pre-warm)
L4.content: the growing history; the previous step's tool_result and the current command are always the last blocks; tenant data, task context from Muneral, receipts, on-demand skill bodies, timestamps and anything volatile live here
forbidden: rewriting earlier messages within a session (compaction = new session with the parent's byte-identical L0–L3)
an explicit breakpoint anywhere but the last content block of the last message

breakpoint.position: last content block of the last message
breakpoint.explicit: optional — when absent the platform's automatic top-level breakpoint is relied on

steps: 1. L0 := request.tools (or [] when absent). Any cache_control on a tool → BREAKPOINT_MISPLACED.
2. system must be a list of blocks; a string system cannot carry breakpoints → SYSTEM_NOT_BLOCKS (and no further derivation for L1..L3; the whole system string is scanned as prefix).
3. Partition the system blocks after every block that carries cache_control. Closed partitions p1, p2, p3 …; blocks after the last breakpoint form an unclosed tail.
4. ≥3 closed partitions: L1=p1, L2=p2, L3=p3; a 4th closed partition or an unclosed tail → BREAKPOINT_MISPLACED.

5. exactly 2 closed partitions and no unclosed tail: L1=p1, L2=p2, L3 := leading text blocks of messages[0] (role user, list content) up to and including the first block with cache_control; when messages[0] has no such leading block → MISSING_BREAKPOINT (L3).
6. 2 closed partitions with an unclosed tail, or fewer than 2 closed partitions → MISSING_BREAKPOINT for each missing layer end.

7. L4 := all remaining message content. Explicit breakpoints in L4 must number ≤1 and sit on the last content block of the last message → else L4_BREAKPOINT_NOT_LAST. Total explicit breakpoints > 4 → BREAKPOINT_EXCESS.
8. TTLs along the prefix (L1, L2, L3, L4) must be in {5m, 1h} (TTL_INVALID) and non-increasing (TTL_ORDER). Absent ttl = 5m.

9. est_tokens(L0..L3) < models[model].min_prefix_tokens → PREFIX_BELOW_MINIMUM (a short prefix is silently not cached: this is a violation, not a warning). Unknown model → MODEL_UNKNOWN, verdict UNDETERMINED.

10. Dynamic-token, identity, tenant and secret scans run over the stable prefix text = L0 canonical JSON + L1..L3 text (when derivation failed: tools + all system blocks). L3 grammar is checked only when L3 was derived.

11. prefix_hash := sha256(canonical_json({tools: L0, L1, L2, L3})) with canonical_json = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False); layer hashes likewise per layer. Computed BEFORE sending; logged with the response usage.

session_rules.SESSION_MODEL_CHANGED: model differs from the session's first request
session_rules.SESSION_TOOLS_CHANGED: the tool SET or any definition differs from the first request
session_rules.SESSION_SYSTEM_CHANGED: L1 or L2 hash differs from the first request
session_rules.SESSION_L3_CHANGED: L3 hash differs from the first request
session_rules.L4_NOT_APPEND_ONLY: the previous request's messages (cache_control stripped) are not a prefix of the current request's messages (equality allowed, e.g. a pre-warm)
session_rules.PREFIX_CHANGED: event (not a code): prefix_hash differs from the previous request; carries the per-layer diff; a session with N hash changes emits exactly N events

fork_rule: subagents, forks and compaction restarts MUST reuse the parent's byte-identical L0–L3 (equal prefix_hash); a compaction summary is a new L4, never a new system prompt
knowledge_loading_rule: skills and project knowledge enter L2 at session start only; loading knowledge mid-session is permitted only as an L4 block (tool_result or user text), which invalidates nothing above messages

by_cadence.cadence: step interval < 5 min and session shorter than ~1 h
by_cadence.note: 5m everywhere is cheapest when the loop never pauses; 1h on L1/L2 pays off when many sessions of the same agent version share them within the hour
a 5m prefix would expire between steps; every step would be a write
expect a write per session; pre-warm with max_tokens=0 right before the step when the step time is known

ttl_policy.invariant: TTL never increases along the prefix (1h before 5m); L3 and L4 are 5m
ttl_policy.keep_warm: a pre-warm request (max_tokens=0) with the identical L0–L3 refreshes the TTL; it must itself pass the linter

model.cache_effect: cache namespace; must not change within a session

tools.cache_effect: first prefix segment; any change invalidates everything

system.cache_effect: second prefix segment; carries the L1/L2(/L3) breakpoints

messages.cache_effect: third segment; append-only; L3 may live in its head

tool_choice.cache_effect: a change invalidates the messages cache (not tools/system)

thinking.cache_effect: a change invalidates messages always; tools/system model-specific

checked_by: session rule SESSION_SYSTEM_CHANGED applies when the toggle changes the system segment; otherwise out of scope of v1 (recorded)

scan_patterns._note: Python `re` patterns; the linter imports them from this file so the gateway (AUP-CACHE-006) can import the same rules instead of duplicating them. Flags: (?i) = case-insensitive.

SYSTEM_NOT_BLOCKS.meaning: system is a string; breakpoints cannot be placed

MISSING_BREAKPOINT.meaning: an end of L1, L2 or L3 carries no cache_control

BREAKPOINT_MISPLACED.meaning: cache_control on a tool, a 4th system partition, or system blocks after the L3 breakpoint

L4_BREAKPOINT_NOT_LAST.meaning: an explicit L4 breakpoint that is not on the last content block of the last message, or more than one in L4

PREFIX_BELOW_MINIMUM.meaning: estimated L0..L3 tokens below the model's minimum cacheable prefix — silently uncached

MODEL_UNKNOWN.meaning: model not in the contract table; minimum unknown; verdict UNDETERMINED

NON_TEXT_IN_PREFIX.meaning: a non-text block (image, document, tool_result) inside L1..L3

DYN_TIMESTAMP.meaning: date-time / 'today is' date / epoch in L0..L3

DYN_UUID.meaning: UUID in L0..L2, or in L3 outside an allowed key

DYN_ENV.meaning: environment-looking value (KEY=VALUE, $HOME, /tmp path, hostname, pid) in L0..L3

USER_IDENTITY_IN_PREFIX.meaning: e-mail, user name or home directory in L0..L3

TENANT_IN_PREFIX.meaning: tenant / workspace / customer marker before the last breakpoint

SECRET_IN_PREFIX.meaning: secret pattern in L0..L3 — the request must not be sent

L3_GRAMMAR.meaning: L3 is not a key: value record / JSON object

SESSION_TOOLS_CHANGED.meaning: tool set or definition changed within a session

TOOL_ORDER_NONDETERMINISTIC.meaning: same tools, different order across requests

SECRET_IN_TAIL.meaning: secret pattern after the last breakpoint (not cached; still reported)

PARAMS_CHANGED.meaning: tool_choice / thinking / effort changed within a session (messages-level invalidation)

verdicts.UNDETERMINED: MODEL_UNKNOWN or unreadable request — a third verdict, never collapsed into either of the others

cli-subscription.examples: Claude Code / Codex CLI sessions on the operator's subscription
cli-subscription.prefix_owner: vendor harness (tools, static system, session metadata are built by the CLI)
cli-subscription.what_we_control: L2 content (CLAUDE.md router, mandates index, skills index) and the discipline not to switch model mid-session; on-demand knowledge only via skills/tool results (L4)
cli-subscription.measurement: indirect only — usage fields are not exposed; recorded as usage_missing in AUP-CACHE-003
cli-subscription.lint_scope: L2 documents (CLAUDE.md, mandates, skill index) scanned with the same patterns
cli-subscription.waiver_reason: the harness itself puts cwd / home paths into its system prompt; the operator cannot remove them, so they are reported, not counted

api-agent-conn.examples: arcana agents (Arcanada Agent System) calling through Model Connector
api-agent-conn.layers: L0 deterministic registry with deferred stubs; L1 role; L2 knowledge pack pinned by digest; L3 {contract, agent, agent_class, agent_version, work_item}; L4 append-only
api-agent-conn.ttl: L1/L2 1h by default, 5m when the profile is fast-loop; L3/L4 5m
api-agent-conn.measurement: CONN per request (AUP-CACHE-003); replay loop mandatory before admission (AUP-CACHE-004/008)

muneral-automation.examples: Muneral event-driven automations (transitions, reminders, evidence attachment)
muneral-automation.layers: as api-agent-conn; the triggering event and the work item payload are L4
muneral-automation.ttl: L1/L2 1h (events are sporadic, 5–60 min gaps typical); L3/L4 5m

publisher.examples: Publisher agents (the only outward publication path per the workspace mandate)
publisher.layers: publication rules and channel formats in L2; schedules, publication dates, post bodies and channel credentials handles are L4 (dates are dynamic by nature)
publisher.ttl: 1h on L1/L2 during a batch; 5m below

adsessor.layers: as api-agent-conn with the strictest tenant rule: every customer / tenant datum is L4; the cache identity at CONN is tenant-scoped (AUP-CACHE-006)

talomnia.layers: domain knowledge pack in L2 pinned by digest; per-conversation material L4

fixtures.naming: conformant-NN-<slug>.json | violation-<CODE>-NN-<slug>.json | undetermined-<CODE>-NN-<slug>.json | a directory of NNN.json files = one session
fixtures.generator: tools/prompt-cache/make_fixtures.py (deterministic; regenerating must reproduce byte-identical files)

failure_conditions: the contract admits a dynamic field in L0–L3
the contract omits the TTL rule
the contract trusts an agent's self-description instead of the bytes of the request
